Key Personalities Associated with Jammu and Kashmir

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Highlights prominent historical and modern personalities associated with Jammu and Kashmir.
Features a One-Line Quick Facts Compendium designed for fast reference.
Provides structured Quick Revision Points for efficient last-minute study.

cells: 8th-century Karkota-dynasty ruler; built the Martand Sun Temple; major territorial expander (Chapter 5)
12th-century chronicler; composed the Rajatarangini, one of ancient India's earliest systematic historical works (Chapter 5)
15th-century Kashmir Sultanate ruler celebrated for religious tolerance and craft patronage (Chapter 6)
Persian Sufi saint of major influence on Kashmiri Islam and crafts; Khanqah-e-Moula shrine (Chapters 6, 20)
Founder of the Dogra princely state via the 1846 Treaty of Amritsar (Chapter 7)
Last ruling Dogra Maharaja; signed the Instrument of Accession to India, 26 October 1947 (Chapter 8)
Founder of the Muslim Conference (1932)/National Conference (1939); first head of J&K's post-accession interim administration; central figure in negotiating Article 370 (Chapters 7, 9)
Indian Constituent Assembly member; principal co-drafter of Article 370 alongside Sheikh Abdullah (Chapter 9)
Son of Sheikh Abdullah; veteran National Conference leader; multiple-time former Chief Minister of the erstwhile state; current national NC president
Grandson of Sheikh Abdullah, son of Farooq Abdullah; former CM of the erstwhile state (2009-2015); first CM of the UT era (since 16 October 2024) — Chapters 16, 25
Current Lieutenant Governor of J&K UT, in office since August 2020 (Chapter 16)
Founder of Kashmir's indigenous Rishi Sufi order; Charar-e-Sharief shrine (Chapters 20, 21)

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: The Abdullah family — Sheikh Abdullah (grandfather), Farooq Abdullah (father), Omar Abdullah (grandson) — spans J&K's entire modern political history from the pre-Independence Muslim/National Conference movement through to the present-day UT government, making this dynastic thread one of the most consistently useful organising narratives across multiple chapters of this book.

items: J&K (UT): approx 42,241 sq km; Srinagar (summer capital), Jammu (winter capital); 20 districts.
Mountain ranges, south to north: Shivalik -> Pir Panjal -> Great Himalaya/Zanskar -> Ladakh Range -> Karakoram (last two mostly in Ladakh UT).
Kashmir Valley: ~135 km x 32 km, ~1,600 m elevation, drained by the Jhelum; 'karewa' terraces used for saffron.
Wular Lake = largest freshwater lake (not Dal Lake); Zoji La connects Kashmir to Ladakh; Banihal Pass connects Jammu to Kashmir.
Indus Waters Treaty (1960): Jhelum & Chenab are 'Western Rivers', predominantly for Pakistan's use.
Kalhana's Rajatarangini (~1148-50 CE); Karkota dynasty's Lalitaditya built the Martand Sun Temple.
Shah Mir founded the Kashmir Sultanate (1339); Mughal conquest (1586); Afghan/Durrani rule (1752-1819); Sikh rule (1819-46).
Treaty of Amritsar (16 March 1846): British sell Kashmir to Gulab Singh for 75 lakh Nanakshahi rupees, founding Dogra rule.
Instrument of Accession signed by Hari Singh: 26 October 1947.
Ceasefire Line (1 Jan 1949) renamed Line of Control by the Simla Agreement (2 July 1972).
Kargil War (1999): Operation Vijay (ground) + Operation Safed Sagar (IAF); Kargil Vijay Diwas = 26 July.
Article 370 (1949): limited automatic Constitution applicability; J&K had its OWN separate Constitution (1957).
Article 35A (1954 Presidential Order): 'Permanent Resident' land/job/settlement rights, restricting non-residents.

5 August 2019: Presidential Order + Parliament resolution effectively abrogate Article 370's operative effect; 9 Aug 2019: Reorganisation Act passed; 31 Oct 2019: takes effect — J&K UT (with Assembly) + Ladakh UT (without Assembly) created.
December 2023 SC verdict: UPHELD abrogation's validity; directed elections by 30 Sept 2024 (met); directed statehood restoration 'at the earliest' (STILL PENDING as of 2026).
'Domicile' status (post-2019) replaced 'Permanent Resident' status (pre-2019); land-purchase restrictions on non-residents removed.
J&K Assembly elections held Sept-Oct 2024; NC-Congress alliance forms government (NC 42/90 seats).
Omar Abdullah = first CM of the UT era (since 16 Oct 2024); Deputy CM Surinder Kumar Choudhary; LG Manoj Sinha (since Aug 2020).
90-seat Assembly + 5 LG-nominated members (incl. Kashmiri-migrant and PoJK-displaced representation).
High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh = single shared High Court for both post-2019 UTs.
Questions frequently target key personalities from Jammu and Kashmir across state-level and national exams.
One-line quick facts are high-yield sources for direct, objective-style exam questions.
J&K = India's largest apple-producing state/UT; Kashmir Saffron and Kashmir Pashmina both GI-tagged.
Kashmiri Pandit exodus began early 1990 — major, sensitive demographic event; 5 nominated Assembly seats partly address representation.
J&K Official Languages Act, 2020: Kashmiri, Dogri, Hindi, Urdu, English all official languages.
Hangul (Kashmir stag) = state animal, critically endangered, found in Dachigam National Park.
Amarnath Yatra (Shri Amarnath Shrine Board) and Vaishno Devi Shrine (Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine Board) = flagship pilgrimages.
USBRL rail link's Chenab Bridge = world's highest railway arch bridge; Anji Khad Bridge = India's first cable-stayed rail bridge.
